title: Representability of fixed generic-fibre free-rank loci
statement: Let $S,X$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $g:X\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically irreducible nonempty fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and let $E$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. For a scheme $T\to S$ put $X_T=X\times_ST$ and let $E_T$ be tensor pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $r\geq0$ define $H_r(T)$ to be a singleton if, for every $t\in T$, $E_T$ is free of rank $r$ on an open neighbourhood in $X_T$ of the unique generic point $\xi_t$ of $(X_T)_t$, and empty otherwise. Free of rank $r$ means isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_T}^{\oplus r}$ on that neighbourhood. A generic point is a point whose closure is the whole fibre [def-sc-generic-point]. Then $H_r$ is represented on all $S$-schemes by a locally closed immersion $S_r\to S$ of finite presentation. A locally closed immersion means a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

source.place: Tag 05UC (lemma-free-at-generic-points-representable), with the functor of situation-free-at-generic-points and equation-free-at-generic-points.

proof.text: We use the following geometry also after arbitrary base change and restriction to source and base opens. Smoothness is preserved by these operations, and implies flatness and local finite presentation. Smooth fibres are geometrically reduced; combined with the assumed geometric irreducibility and nonemptiness this makes every fibre geometrically integral. Thus its generic point has a field as its local ring within the fibre. Define $p(s)=\dim_{\kappa(\xi_s)}(E_{\xi_s}\otimes\kappa(\xi_s))$. For $t\mapsto s$, the generic point of $X_t$ maps to that of $X_s$: on affine fibre rings the field extension gives an injective map of domains, and localization to their fraction fields still is injective. Tensoring a vector-space basis with the resulting field extension shows $p(t)=p(s)$. Here all sheaf pullbacks have the tensor description on affine opens. Consequently $H_r(T)$ implies $p(h(t))=r$ for every $t\in T$. Pulling back a free neighbourhood preserves freeness and contains the new generic point, so $H_r$ is stable under arbitrary base change. Its predicate is Zariski local on $T$, directly from its neighbourhood definition.

source.place: Tag 05UC, generic fibre ranks paragraph; situation-free-at-generic-points and equation-free-at-generic-points

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $M=\Gamma(X,E)$. The affine finite-presentation criterion makes $M$ finitely presented, hence finitely generated. A finite generating list of length $N$ gives $p(s)\leq N$ for all $s$. Fix $s$. Choose $p(s)$ elements of $M$ whose images are a basis of $M\otimes_B\kappa(\xi_s)$, by selecting a basis from the images of a generating list. Stalks are module localizations, and Nakayama over $B_{\xi_s}$ says these elements generate $M_{\xi_s}$. The cokernel of their map $B^{\oplus p(s)}\to M$ is finitely generated and vanishes on localization at $\xi_s$. Each of finitely many cokernel generators is killed by an element outside $\xi_s$; their product $b\notin\xi_s$ kills the cokernel. We have a surjection $\mathcal O_{D(b)}^{\oplus p(s)}\twoheadrightarrow E|_{D(b)}$. The image of $D(b)$ in $S$ is open, since $g$ is flat and locally finitely presented. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V_s$ of $s$ inside this image, and put $U_s=D(b)\times_S V_s$. Both $U_s,V_s$ are affine. Their morphism is smooth, has nonempty geometrically integral fibres, and carries the displayed generating surjection. For each $t\in V_s$, its fibre open $U_{s,t}$ is nonempty and has the same generic point as $X_t$. This remains true after any base change. Therefore restricting to $U_s$ leaves every $H_r$ unchanged over $V_s$, and $p(t)\leq p(s)$ there.

source.place: Tag 05UC, open-source replacement and local generating-surjection paragraphs

proof.text: Consider any such chart $U\to V$ with a fixed surjection $u:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow E|_U$. Its global-isomorphism predicate after base change equals $H_n$. Only the forward implication needs work. Test on affine opens $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of an arbitrary $V$-scheme. Write $U_T=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $L=\Gamma(U_T,E_T)$. The affine flatness and presentation criteria make $R\to C$ flat and finitely presented; its fibres are geometrically integral and nonempty by step 1. The tensor pullback formula and preservation of finite module presentation make $L$ finitely presented. Suppose $H_n(T)$ holds. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p C$ is prime and contracts to $\mathfrak p$: $C/\mathfrak pC=C\otimes_RR/\mathfrak p$ is flat over the domain $R/\mathfrak p$, hence torsion-free, so it embeds into its localization $C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the fibre ring, which is a nonzero domain; torsion-freeness of this nonzero module also makes $R/\mathfrak p\to C/\mathfrak pC$ injective. At $\mathfrak q$, $L_{\mathfrak q}$ is free of rank $n$ over $C_{\mathfrak q}$; it is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ by smooth flatness. The localized surjection is an isomorphism: in chosen bases it is a surjective square matrix, whose right inverse makes its determinant a unit, so its adjugate gives an inverse. In particular its residue-field map is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-local-flat-generic-basis-universal-injectivity] at $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$. On some $D(f)$ containing $\mathfrak p$ the specified $u$ is universally injective over $R_f$, hence injective by taking the tensor test module $R_f$. It remains surjective, so is an isomorphism there. These $D(f)$ cover $T$, proving $u_T$ is an isomorphism. Conversely an isomorphism $u_T$ trivializes $E_T$ everywhere on $U_T$ and immediately implies $H_n(T)$.

source.place: Tag 05UC, equality with F_iso; Tag 05IA (lemma-induction-step-fp), implication (1) to (2)

proof.text: For $n=p(s)$ apply [lem-sfb-flat-integral-free-surjection-iso-locus] to $U_s\to V_s$ and its generating surjection. Flatness and finite presentation follow from smoothness and the affine criteria used in step 3; the source is affine over the affine base and the target module is finitely presented. This gives a closed immersion of finite presentation representing $H_{p(s)}$ over $V_s$, by step 3. For $q>p(s)$, $H_q$ over $V_s$ is the empty functor: a nonempty test scheme satisfying it would have a point $t$ with $q=p(h(t))\leq p(s)$, a contradiction. On the empty test scheme both predicates hold vacuously, as does factorization through the empty scheme.

We prove, simultaneously for all $r$, representability by a finitely presented locally closed immersion over every quasi-compact open $B\subseteq S$, by induction on an upper bound $m$ for $p$ on $B$. Such a $B$ has a finite cover by principal affine opens of $S$, with affine intersections, so is quasi-separated. The empty $B$ is immediate. For a nonempty $B$ take the actual maximum $m$; it exists by the finite bound $N$ in step 2. At a point with $p(s)=m$, step 4 gives a closed finitely presented representative of $H_m$ on a neighbourhood inside $B$. At a point with $p(s)<m$, it gives the empty representative on a neighbourhood. Apply [lem-sc-local-finitely-presented-immersion-locus] using the base-change stability and source-locality proved in step 1, to glue these representatives to an immersion $Z_m\to B$ locally of finite presentation. All its base restrictions just constructed are closed immersions. Closed immersion is local on the target, so $Z_m\to B$ is closed. Its local defining ideals are of finite type by [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal]; these local finite-generation statements give a finite-type ideal sheaf on $B$, and the same criterion shows $Z_m\to B$ is of finite presentation. Its underlying set is exactly $\{s:p(s)=m\}$: the residue-field test at $s$ belongs to $H_{p(s)}$, indeed on the affine integral fibre choose lifts of a basis over its fraction field. Their map from a finite free module to the finitely presented fibre module is bijective at the zero prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-to-finitely-presented-map-iso-at-prime-spreads] it is bijective after inverting a nonzero element, giving a free neighbourhood of the fibre generic point. It cannot belong to another $H_r$, by step 1.

source.place: Tag 05UC, maximum-rank induction paragraph and final finite-presentation paragraph

proof.text: The open complement $B'=B\setminus |Z_m|$ is quasi-compact. Indeed take a finite affine cover of $B$. On each member the ideal of $Z_m$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type by the ideal criterion in step 5, so its sections there form a finitely generated ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a), so its complement is a finite union of principal opens. Each principal open is affine and quasi-compact, and a finite union of such spaces is quasi-compact. Now $p\leq m-1$ on $B'$. If $m=0$, $B'$ is empty and all $H_r$ except $H_0$ are empty. Otherwise apply the induction hypothesis to $B'$, a quasi-compact open of the original affine $S$. For $r<m$, the predicate $H_r(T)$ for $T\to B$ forces the image of every point into $B'$, by step 1. The open-factorization lemma then factors this map uniquely through $B'$. Conversely a test map through $B'$ has exactly the same generic-freeness predicate there. Thus the representative supplied by induction over $B'$ also represents $H_r$ over $B$. For $r>m$ the functor is empty, and $r=m$ was settled in step 5.

source.place: Tag 05UC, rank induction and quasi-compact-open-complement argument

proof.text: The inclusion $B'\hookrightarrow B$ in step 6 is finitely presented: apply [lem-nagata-qc-open-basechanged-affine-chart-fp] with its base $S$ the original affine $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, its test scheme $T=B$, its affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ the identity, and its quasi-compact open $W=B'\subseteq X_T=B$. The needed quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $B$ were checked in step 5. Composition preserves finite presentation and immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], clauses (d) and (e). Hence every representative inherited from $B'$ is a finitely presented locally closed immersion into $B$. This completes the induction. Finally take $B=S$, which is quasi-compact since affine, to obtain $S_r\to S$ for every $r\geq0$. All comparisons were on arbitrary test schemes, using affine open covers only to test module isomorphisms, so this represents $H_r$ on all $S$-schemes, including nonreduced and nonaffine ones.
